topic: How can beamforming and transponder allocation adapt to dynamic Doppler shifts in LEO mega-constellations for SC-FDMA uplinks?
consensus_response: To mitigate the effects of dynamic Doppler shifts in LEO mega-constellations, adaptive beamforming techniques can be employed to adjust beam direction and shape in real-time based on user terminal mobility and satellite movement. This adaptation introduces additional latency due to continuous beam recalibration. To address this challenge, advanced modulation techniques can be used to adapt to changing channel conditions without requiring continuous beam recalibration, mitigating the trade-off between bandwidth allocation and beamforming adaptation.
reference_context: The maximum Doppler shift for a 500 km/h relative user mobility at 20 GHz is approximately 9.3 kHz, necessitating larger subcarrier spacing and transponder allocations to compensate for increased interference and signal degradation.
